etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English alive, alife, olive, olife, on live, on life, from Old English on līfe (“alive”, literally “in life" or "in (the) body”), from on (“on, in”) + līfe, dative singular of līf (“life”). In this sense, replaced Old English cwic (whence English quick). Equivalent to a- +‎ life. Compare Dutch in leven (“alive”, literally “in life”), German am Leben (“alive”, literally “at life" or "at living”).

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Rev 1:18:
quote.text: I am hee that liueth, and was dead : and behold, I am aliue foꝛ euermoꝛe,Amen,and haue the keyes of hell and of death.

definitions.definition: In a state of action; in force or operation; existent.
Busy with activity of many living beings; swarming; thronged; busy.

quote.citation: 1848, Thomas Babington Macaulay, The History of England from the Accession of James the Second:
quote.text: The Boyne, for a quarter of a mile, was alive with muskets and green boughs.

definitions.definition: (of electrical wiring) Carrying electrical current; energized.
(in the construction "alive to") Aware of; sensitive to.

quote.citation: 1925, Godfrey W. Mathews, The Chester Mystery Plays  […] ., Liverpool: Edward Howell LTD, page 5:
quote.text: We may be sure that the Church would be alive to the dangers of allowing the plays to be performed outside the sacred edifice.

quote.citation: 1836 March – 1837 October, Charles Dickens, “(please specify the chapter name)”, in The Posthumous Papers of the Pickwick Club, London: Chapman and Hall, […], published 1837, →OCLC:
quote.text: Smouch, requesting Mr. Pickwick in a surly manner ‘to be as alive as he could, for it was a busy time,’ drew up a chair by the door and sat there, until he had finished dressing.

quote.citation: 2018 May 26, Daniel Taylor, “Liverpool go through after Mohamed Salah stops Manchester City fightback”, in The Guardian (London)‎[1]:
quote.text: Liverpool’s equaliser came within four minutes. James Milner swung the ball over from a corner on the right and Sadio Mané, Liverpool’s most dangerous player, was alive in the six-yard area.

definitions.definition: Susceptible, sensitive; easy to impress; having keen feelings, as opposed to apathy.

quote.text: Though tremblingly alive to Nature's laws, Yet ever firm to Honour's sacred cause

quote.citation: 1887, Robert Louis Stevenson, “Pastoral”, in Memories and Portraits, New York: Charles Scribner, page 99:
quote.text: This was a reproach to John, and a slur upon the dog; and both were alive to their misfortune.

quote.citation: 1702, Edward Hyde Clarendon, The History of the Rebellion:
quote.text: The Earl of Northumberland 'was the proudest man alive' and 'was in all his deportment a very great man.

quote.citation: 2000, Candye Kane (lyrics and music), “The Toughest Girl Alive”:
quote.text: I'm the toughest girl alive / I walked through the fire and I survived.
